report:
[ORACLE] Upgrade

Hello, Chris.
I hope this message finds you well.
Today, I bring you another problem that has arisen with the latest version of Debezium.
As you probably know, our Debezium Source connector is implemented with ‘log.mining.strategy’: ‘hybrid’ to handle the mixture of DDL and DML. The DDL is propagated in parallel, with python, and the sink connectors are reset to work correctly. This strategy has worked perfectly so far. In addition, we have also defined the PostSelector strategy (which already has the problem fixed) to propagate LOB types to the Sink Database.
After this context, the problem is as follows:
We're currently testing the new version (3.1.1) and adapting our update algorithm so that everything is automated.
So the problem seems to be with the Sink Connector. Before this new version, we ran the script on the source database, the collected source dealt with the mixture of DDL + DML and the drain connector showed an error relating to the evolution of the schema, which was to be expected. After that, we propagated the DDL with python, restarted the sink and everything worked correctly.
With this version, the sink connector has another error in addition to the schema evolution error, which is :
Caused by: org.apache.kafka.connect.errors.ConnectException: Error while checking and applying table changes for collection ‘{}’, even after the DDL script have been propagated to the sink database
In addition, only the table that requires the PostSelector strategy works correctly. We don't know if there is any correlation here.
Do you have any ideas about this? Is the changed code not working as it was supposed to?
I've attached the log file.
Best regards,
Vitor Pereira
upgrade_log.txt

evidence.quote: your python script is effectively getting ahead of itself and changing the table structure too early. This isn't a Debezium issue." Reporter later: "it solved the problem.

notes: Sink schema evolution only adds columns; renaming the target column before buffered events (multi-partition, offset flush timing) were consumed triggers 'schema evolution is disabled'. Code in JdbcChangeEventSink.alterTableIfNeeded shows intended behavior.
